Treatment summary
Patient presented following a rear impact sustained while the vehicle was turning
left, with complaints of neck pain, stiffness, and headache consistent with a cervical
strain. The mechanism and force of the collision align well with the injury described.
Over the course of 27 visits, care icnluded soft tissue treatment, range-of-motion
exercises, and home stretching instructions. Progress followed a typical recovery
pattern, with visit frequency decreasing as symptoms improved and range of motion
returned. Examination documented reduced cervical range of motion and paraspinal
tenderness, supporting the diagnosis, while several neurological screening tests were
within normal limits. The patient reported a remote, minor strain to the same region
years earlier, which had resolved completely without lasting limitation. Billing
records reflect single, appropriate charges for each service rendered, with no
duplicated entries. Patinet was discharged to self-directed home exercise with
instructions to return if symptoms recur.

Person "role" must be one of: claimant, attorney, defense_attorney, expert, doctor, officer, adjuster, witness, other.
  claimant = the person who made the claim (also called patient, plaintiff, client, customer,
  or the driver who reported it). attorney = a lawyer for the claimant or plaintiff.
  defense_attorney = a lawyer for the insurance company or defendant.
Organization "type" must be one of: repair_shop, clinic, law_firm, court, insurer, police, other.
"policy_numbers" = only values labeled as a policy number. A claim number is not a policy number.
"street" and "city" = the person's own home address, only if the page gives it. Never use the
address of a clinic, shop, firm or court for a person.
"loss_dates" = only a date that the page clearly gives as the date of the accident, crash, loss or
injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
